questions.prompt: Fearing that anyone might see her, the woman fled through the night gate.
questions.answer: Timēns nē quis sē vidēret, fēmina per portam nocturnam fūgit.

questions.prompt: Death, as the philosophers teach, is a kind of transfer, as it were.
questions.answer: Mors, ut philosophī docent, quasi quaedam migrātiō est.

questions.prompt: The general was pondering something great in his mind while he walked silently.
questions.answer: Aliquid magnum animō volvēbat dux, cum tacitus ambulāret.

questions.prompt: If we must spare anyone, let us spare the conquered enemies.
questions.answer: Sī cui parcendum est, hostibus victīs parcāmus.

questions.prompt: A certain merchant came to me, carrying dates from Syria.
questions.answer: Vēnit ad mē quīdam mercātor, caryotās ex Syriā portāns.

questions.prompt: Does anyone doubt that virtue alone is praiseworthy?
questions.answer: Num quis dubitat quīn virtūs sōla laudābilis sit?

questions.prompt: Give me something that may refresh my sick soul.
questions.answer: Dā mihī aliquid quod animum aegrum recreet.

questions.prompt: Unless someone helps us, we will not be able to defend the abandoned city.
questions.answer: Nisi quis nōs adiuvābit, urbem relictam dēfendere nōn poterimus.

questions.prompt: A certain judge, although stern, spared the wretched plebs.
questions.answer: Quīdam iūdex, quamquam sevērus, plēbī miserae pepercit.

questions.prompt: If anyone asks you, say that I am working in the fields.
questions.answer: Sī quis tē rogābit, dīc mē in agrīs labōrāre.

questions.prompt: There was a sort of royal dignity, as it were, in his face.
questions.answer: Erat quaedam quasi rēgia dignitās in vultū eius.

questions.prompt: If anyone thinks that virtue is an easy thing, let him try it.
questions.answer: Sī quis virtūtem facilem esse putat, cōnētur.

questions.prompt: Unless someone comes to the aid of the exhausted soldiers, the city will fall.
questions.answer: Nisi quis fessīs mīlitibus subvenerit, urbs cadet.

questions.prompt: Lest anyone hear the secret plan, they kept talking in whispers.
questions.answer: Nē quis arcānum cōnsilium audīret, susurrīs loquēbantur.

questions.prompt: He asked whether anyone had seen the fugitive fleeing.
questions.answer: Rogāvit num quis fugitīvum fugientem vīdisset.

questions.prompt: If anyone should creep toward the walls, let the guards resist him.
questions.answer: Sī quis ad mūrōs rēpat, custōdēs resistant.

questions.prompt: Somebody consoled the girl torn by grief.
questions.answer: Aliquis puellam maerōre laniātam cōnsōlātus est.

questions.prompt: A certain shame keeps me from confessing the crime.
questions.answer: Pudor quīdam mē scelus cōnfitērī prohibet.

questions.prompt: Lest anything bad happen, the far-sighted general marked out the camp.
questions.answer: Nē quid malī accidat, dux prōvidus castra dēsignāvit.

questions.prompt: If anyone had listened to the learned orator, he would have understood something new.
questions.answer: Sī quis ōrātōrem doctum audīvisset, aliquid novum intellēxisset.

questions.prompt: A certain philosopher used to discuss virtue in the forum every day.
questions.answer: Philosophus quīdam dē virtūte in forō cotīdiē disserēbat.

questions.prompt: Let somebody bring wine, so that we may taste its sweetness.
questions.answer: Aliquis vīnum ferat, ut eius sapōrem gūstēmus.

questions.prompt: Death is, as it were, a certain journey to another life.
questions.answer: Mors est quasi quaedam migrātiō ad aliam vītam.

questions.prompt: If anyone thinks the state can stand without laws, he is mistaken.
questions.answer: Sī quis putat rem pūblicam sine lēgibus stāre posse, errat.

questions.prompt: Let somebody bring the letters which the messenger left behind.
questions.answer: Aliquis afferat epistulās quās nūntius relīquit.

questions.prompt: A certain old man, wise beyond his years, warned us about the storm.
questions.answer: Senex quīdam, ultrā annōs sapiēns, dē tempestāte nōs monuit.

questions.prompt: Justice never harms anyone who follows the truth.
questions.answer: Iūstitia numquam cuiquam nocet quī vēritātem sequitur.

questions.prompt: All the best citizens defended the republic in that dangerous time.
questions.answer: Optimus quisque cīvis illō perīculōsō tempore rem pūblicam dēfendit.

questions.prompt: Every fifth year the priests used to renew the sacred games.
questions.answer: Quīntō quōque annō sacerdōtēs lūdōs sacrōs renovābant.

questions.prompt: No mortal can escape death, however powerful he may be.
questions.answer: Nēmō mortālis mortem effugere potest, quamvīs potēns sit.

questions.prompt: Whatever falls to each by lot, let him bear it bravely.
questions.answer: Quod cuique sorte obtigit, id fortiter ferat.

questions.prompt: If any hope remains, we ought to defend the walls fiercely.
questions.answer: Sī qua spēs manet, mūrōs ācriter dēfendere dēbēmus.

questions.prompt: Was this tyrant crueler than any of the earlier kings?
questions.answer: Num hic tyrannus crūdēlior fuit quam quisquam superiōrum rēgum?

questions.prompt: Somebody had hidden the stolen gold beneath the ancient oak.
questions.answer: Aliquis aurum surreptum sub arbore vetustā abdiderat.

questions.prompt: There was a sort of madness, as it were, in the words of the raging prophet.
questions.answer: Īnerat quaedam quasi īnsānia in verbīs vātis furentis.

questions.prompt: Unless someone opens the gates, the ambassadors will not be able to enter.
questions.answer: Nisi quis portās aperiet, lēgātī intrāre nōn poterunt.

questions.prompt: Can anyone endure such great insults without anger?
questions.answer: Num quisquam tantās contumēliās sine īrā ferre potest?

questions.prompt: A certain woman, moved by pity, freed the captive slaves.
questions.answer: Mulier quaedam, misericordiā mōta, captīvōs servōs līberāvit.

questions.prompt: Each best man surpasses the rest in wisdom and courage.
questions.answer: Optimus quisque cēterōs sapientiā et virtūte superat.

questions.prompt: Lest anyone betray the plan, the leaders swore.
questions.answer: Nē quis cōnsilium prōderet, ducēs iūrāvērunt.

questions.prompt: If anybody was ever brave, Horatius was brave at the bridge.
questions.answer: Sī quisquam fortis fuit, Horātius in ponte fortis fuit.

questions.prompt: Someone must announce to the king that the enemy is approaching.
questions.answer: Aliquis rēgī nūntiet hostem appropinquāre.

questions.prompt: No Roman would have surrendered his arms to the barbarians.
questions.answer: Nēmō Rōmānus arma barbarīs trādidisset.

questions.prompt: A certain kind of friendship binds those who love the same studies.
questions.answer: Quaedam amīcitia eōs iungit quī eadem studia dīligunt.

questions.prompt: If you should ask anyone in the forum, he would praise the consul.
questions.answer: Sī quemquam in forō rogēs, cōnsulem laudet.

questions.prompt: Some god, I believe, saved the fleet from the raging waves.
questions.answer: Aliquī deus, ut crēdō, classem ex undīs saevientibus servāvit.

questions.prompt: Let each man defend his own fields against the robbers.
questions.answer: Suōs quisque agrōs contrā praedōnēs dēfendat.

questions.prompt: The cohorts, if any had given ground, he decimated and fed on barley.
questions.answer: Cohortēs, sī quae cessissent locō, decimātās hordeō pāvit.

source.author: Suetonius
source.work: De vita Caesarum Vita divi Augusti

questions.prompt: To each his own is beautiful.
questions.answer: Suum cuique pulchrum est.

questions.prompt: Justice never does harm to anybody.
questions.answer: Iūstitia numquam nocet cuiquam.

questions.prompt: A sage, he was.
questions.answer: Sī quisquam, ille sapiēns fuit.

questions.prompt: If any man is timorous, I am he.
questions.answer: Sī quisquam est timidus, is ego sum.

questions.prompt: Both armies go away, every man to his home.
questions.answer: Ambō exercitūs suās quisque abeunt domōs.

questions.prompt: Each army was in sight of the other.
questions.answer: Uterque utrīque erat exercitus in cōnspectū.

questions.prompt: Set before your eyes each of the kings.
questions.answer: Pōnite ante oculōs ūnum quemque rēgum.

questions.prompt: The wisest men die with the greatest equanimity.
questions.answer: Sapientissimus quisque aequissimō animō moritur.

questions.prompt: For how many would have done this?
questions.answer: Quotus enim istud quisque fēcisset?

questions.prompt: One party fights, the other fears the victor.
questions.answer: Alterī dīmicant, alterī victōrem timent.

questions.prompt: He had ordered each to support the other.
questions.answer: Alteram alterī praesidiō esse iusserat.

questions.prompt: Some make an attack with swords, others with fragments of the railings.
questions.answer: Aliī gladiīs adoriuntur, aliī fragmentīs saeptōrum.

questions.prompt: They ask each other the reason.
questions.answer: Alius ex aliō causam quaerit.

questions.prompt: It is one thing to slander, another to accuse.
questions.answer: Aliud est maledīcere, aliud accūsāre.

questions.prompt: He ordered different persons to dig in different places.
questions.answer: Iussit aliōs alibī fodere.

questions.prompt: Some halted in one place, some in another.
questions.answer: Aliī aliō locō resistēbant.

questions.prompt: The laws are silent in time of war.
questions.answer: Silent lēgēs inter arma.

questions.prompt: You, who know, will use all diligence.
questions.answer: Tū, quī scīs, omnem dīligentiam adhibēbis.

questions.prompt: See how all of us are scorned who are from the free towns.
questions.answer: Vidēte quam dēspiciāmur omnēs quī sumus ē mūnicipiīs.

questions.prompt: Not every error should be called folly.
questions.answer: Nōn omnis error stultitia dīcenda est.

questions.prompt: The general and several leading men are taken.
questions.answer: Dux cum aliquot prīncipibus capiuntur.

questions.prompt: The Roman senate and people understand.
questions.answer: Senātus populusque Rōmānus intellegit.

questions.prompt: The reputation and life of an innocent man are defended.
questions.answer: Fāma et vīta innocentis dēfenditur.

questions.prompt: Mark Antony and Quintus Cassius, tribunes of the people, interpose.
questions.answer: Intercēdit M. Antōnius Q. Cassius tribūnī plēbis.

questions.prompt: This both the Peripatetic philosophers and the Old Academy grant me.
questions.answer: Hōc mihi et Peripatēticī et vetus Acadēmia concēdit.

questions.prompt: The army returns to winter-quarters.
questions.answer: Ad hīberna exercitus redit.

questions.prompt: The plebs seceded from the patricians.
questions.answer: Plēbēs ā patribus sēcessit.

questions.prompt: He sent ahead all the cavalry he had, to see.
questions.answer: Equitātum omnem . . . quem habēbat praemittit, quī videant.

questions.prompt: They fought long and vigorously.
questions.answer: Diū atque ācriter pūgnātum est.

questions.prompt: There may often occur a comparison of two honorable actions, as to which is the more honorable.
questions.answer: Potest incidere saepe contentiō et comparātiō dē duōbus honestīs utrum honestius.
